label: EU OEE Fact write
info: Writes EU_OEE_Fact (65 columns, one file per site, day and record type) from the rows of PBI report build, PBI report build 2 and Chartres live. Needs the Config tab.

name: [1] WRITE EU_OEE_FACT
info: STAGE 1 - one table message of a build tab arrives through the link in eu-oee-fact WRITE (the rows that table writes to report/). 1 FACT SETTINGS holds DRY_RUN (true: nothing is written, the log shows what would be) MONTH_JOBS (false: a month job of a build tab writes no fact file, the month files hold the history) and FIRST_DAY (no fact file before the cutover day) and sets the line list file report/Dim/Machine_Names_EU.csv, which is read and parsed. 2 maps the rows to the 65 columns of EU_OEE_Fact: Loss renames (Date -> Event Date, ShiftStartDate -> Date, Shift colour -> Shift Colour, target -> Loss Target), In EU Report Source = the flag of the table, In EU Report = the line is in the line list, Dept / Area / Product Type from the line list (else the row). Then decide, parquet (every column typed, also when empty), the path <root>/report/EU_OEE_Fact/site=<Site>/EU_OEE_Fact_<day>_<plan|tu|loss|rr>_<source>.parquet and write object. A rerun replaces the file.

name: 1.1 FACT SETTINGS (edit here)
1.2 Map to fact columns
1.3 Decide EU_OEE_Fact
1.4 Set fact file path
[2] ERRORS
info: STAGE 2 - a catch node takes every error raised by a node of this tab and turns it into a log line with the name of the node and the message of the API (for example the limit message of evaluateKPIs). Errors of the log nodes themselves are not logged again.

name: 2.1 Describe error
[3] LOG
info: STAGE 3 - every log line arrives here through the link "to LOG". 1 turns a line into a row (time, flow, site, production day, level) and shows it in the debug sidebar. The join collects the rows for 30 s, the delay lets one batch pass every 10 s so two writes do not overlap, 3 sets the file of the month and the read node loads the old file. A read of a file that does not exist answers nothing (only a warning), so the same batch also goes through a 10 s wait to the append step. The log is written whatever the dry-run switch says.

name: 3.1 Format log line
3.2 Note last log line
3.3 Build log write
[4] LOG WRITE
info: STAGE 4 - adds the rows of the batch to the old file and writes the whole file back (the data lake has no append). Columns: ts_utc, seq, flow, site, production_day, mode, level, source, message. Every field is quoted, line breaks become a space. The batch arrives twice (read answer and the wait) and is written once. If the read gives no answer for a file this flow wrote before, a new file with a time stamp is written, so the history is never replaced.
